newsitem.title: MEXICO: TMM says Q2 net loss on new ventures.
newsitem.headline: TMM says Q2 net loss on new ventures.

text.p: Mexican shipping leader Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) said that it lost $2.7 million in the second quarter as it consolidated new business.
"The net loss for the second quarter was $2.7 million after a loss of $3.0 million in the TFM railroad," TMM said in a statement.
Separately, Bear Stearns analyst Santiago Pique said in a report that the loss in TMM's 37.6 percent share in its railroad interest added to continued losses in Far East operations.
The consolidation of fleet Flota Grancolombiana and Compania Trastlantica Espanola also cut into TMM's profits.
But TMM said it managed to show improvements in most operations for June.
Bear Stearns' Pique said in the report that "the improvements, if sustainable, together with the agreement with APL (in Far East shipping), should help the company going forward."

Still, Pique sees a three-cent loss per American Depositary Receipt (ADR) for the year, which he recently revised downward after TMM adjusted down its railroad operations estimates for a 1997 loss of almost #9 million.

Morgan Stanley Dean Witter analyst John Irish said the third quarter report will be helped by the company's APL joint venture. "It basically removed TMM from the worst part of its business," Irish said.
TMM predicted the venture will result in a $17 million to $19 million gross profit in the second half, Irish said.
The company shipped 55.2 percent more in the first half to 256,100 TEUs, compared with the year-ago period. Investors

did not appear pleased with the second quarter loss, however, as the company's shares plunged 7.7 percent to 41.3 pesos from 47.5 pesos on Tuesday. It improved 0.70 peso on Wednesday to close at 42 pesos.
